searchText: <@!552133098075193354> I mentioned some time ago that I want to write an example 1559 fee oracle algorithm using `eth_feeHistory`. Here it is, though honestly I don't know yet for sure how well it will perform with actual market data but we'll have to wait for the actual market to find it out 🙂 Maybe some fine tuning will be needed but in the meantime I just wanted to share it as a WIP version. https://github.com/zsfelfoldi/ethereum-docs/blob/master/eip1559/feeHistory_example.js Please also note that the `eth_feeHistory` result field names were incorrect in the API implementation on our master branch, fixed by this (yet unmerged) PR: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/23178 (my javascript code already uses the correct field names so currently it will only work with the above branch) <@!202397237962211328> That is awesome, many thanks, if you don't mind I am going to port it to Nethereum and add it as an fee calculation strategy. has any research been done on the approximate time needed for the post1559 fee market to stabilize? (asking from the perspective of the miner and future validator) i suspect it will be well within the first hour .. (but this also assumes all miners expand the gas limit to 30MM) it really depends what you mean by stabilize, and depends on several variables, including - tx demand heading into the fork - whether all miners update and maintain the same block gas limit (like you mentioned) > the baseFeePerGas will be set to 1 gwei. This means that, at first, transactions will be competing via a first-price auction on the tip, as the baseFeePerGas reaches the rate where there is ~15m gas /100% demand at that price. > > If you assume the market price is 250 gwei on the fork date, this means that baseFeePerGas needs to go through ~50 blocks to get there, or slightly less than 15 minutes. obviously we are no longer in a 250 gwei regime, so this should be lower. read more here on the Cheatsheet I put together with Tim: https://hackmd.io/4YVYKxxvRZGDto7aq7rVkg?view This is cool! Thank you. Just wondering, is it possible for the mining pool operators to decide on how many txs to include in a block? Cause if that is so, they can be able to manipulate BASEFEE in a way by purposely not filling up the block to the max when they mine the block This has been extensively analysed and the conclusion is that they can't achieve anything by doing this and it will just cost them money. If they have more than 51% of miners colluding they can start causing problems, but the entire security of Ethereum depends on 51% of miners not colluding anyway.

excerpts.author: zsfelfoldi
excerpts.content:
<@!552133098075193354> I mentioned some time ago that I want to write an example 1559 fee oracle algorithm using `eth_feeHistory`. Here it is, though honestly I don't know yet for sure how well it will perform with actual market data but we'll have to wait for the actual market to find it out 🙂 Maybe some fine tuning will be needed but in the meantime I just wanted to share it as a WIP version.
https://github.com/zsfelfoldi/ethereum-docs/blob/master/eip1559/feeHistory_example.js
Please also note that the `eth_feeHistory` result field names were incorrect in the API implementation on our master branch, fixed by this (yet unmerged) PR: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/23178
(my javascript code already uses the correct field names so currently it will only work with the above branch)

excerpts.author: juanblanco
excerpts.content: <@!202397237962211328> That is awesome, many thanks, if you don't mind I am going to port it to Nethereum and add it as an fee calculation strategy.

excerpts.author: mrabino1
excerpts.content: has any research been done on the approximate time needed for the post1559 fee market to stabilize?  (asking from the perspective of the miner and future validator)

excerpts.author: mrabino1
excerpts.content: i suspect it will be well within the first hour .. (but this also assumes all miners expand the gas limit to 30MM)

excerpts.author: trent_vanepps
excerpts.content:
it really depends what you mean by stabilize, and depends on several variables, including 

- tx demand heading into the fork
- whether all miners update and maintain the same block gas limit (like you mentioned)

excerpts.author: trent_vanepps
excerpts.content:
> the baseFeePerGas will be set to 1 gwei. This means that, at first, transactions will be competing via a first-price auction on the tip, as the baseFeePerGas reaches the rate where there is ~15m gas /100% demand at that price.
> 
> If you assume the market price is 250 gwei on the fork date, this means that baseFeePerGas needs to go through ~50 blocks to get there, or slightly less than 15 minutes.

obviously we are no longer in a 250 gwei regime, so this should be lower. read more here on the Cheatsheet I put together with Tim: https://hackmd.io/4YVYKxxvRZGDto7aq7rVkg?view
